summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: Intermittent J12 disconnects under vibration are reported but unmeasured; no vibration test, retention-force measurement, candidate datasheet or independent review exists, so no connector change can be approved for release yet.

sourceRegister.name: Field observation note — Rover Alpha J12 (synthetic)

anchors.excerpt: Operators reported intermittent J12 connector disconnects during vibration on the test track on three separate days.
Each report describes the drive controller losing its link to the sensor harness for one to three seconds and then recovering.
No measured test result is supplied with this note. No vibration profile, accelerometer data or connector retention measurement was recorded.
The reports do not identify whether the J12 shell, the contacts or the harness strain relief released.
Constraint R1: Any connector change must preserve the existing board pinout so the controller firmware and the sensor harness remain unchanged.
Constraint R2: The replacement, if any, must be compatible with the existing drive controller board footprint.
The exact baseline revision of the controller board is not supplied in this note.
The pin mapping table and the compatibility measurements for any candidate connector are not supplied in this note.
Checklist item 1: Vibration-test result for the current J12 connector — ABSENT. No vibration test has been run or recorded.
Checklist item 2: Connector retention-force measurement — not recorded.
Checklist item 3: Candidate replacement connector datasheet — not supplied.
Checklist item 4: Independent engineering review — an independent engineering reviewer has not approved the change.
Note: Items marked absent or not recorded block any release decision until evidence is obtained.

knownFacts.statement: Operators reported intermittent J12 connector disconnects during vibration on the test track on three separate days.
Each report describes the drive controller losing its link to the sensor harness for one to three seconds and then recovering.
No measured test result, vibration profile, accelerometer data or connector retention measurement was recorded with the observation.
Constraint R1: any connector change must preserve the existing board pinout so controller firmware and sensor harness remain unchanged.
Constraint R2: any replacement must be compatible with the existing drive controller board footprint.
An independent engineering reviewer has not approved the change, and absent or unrecorded checklist items block any release decision until evidence is obtained.

alternatives.title: Retain and investigate the current J12 connector
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 and determine the failure mode (shell, contacts or harness strain relief) through vibration testing and retention-force measurement. Whether the current connector is adequate is unknown until evidenced.
prerequisites: Vibration test of the current J12 under a defined test-track profile
Inspection to identify whether shell, contacts or strain relief released

alternatives.title: Evaluate a replacement J12 connector
alternatives.description: Identify a candidate connector that preserves the existing pinout and the drive controller board footprint. No candidate is named; compatibility is unknown until datasheet, pin mapping and compatibility measurements are supplied.
prerequisites: Pin mapping table confirming pinout preservation (R1)
Footprint compatibility evidence against the drive controller board (R2)
Vibration and retention testing of the candidate

evidenceGaps.gap: No vibration-test result for the current J12 connector; no vibration profile or accelerometer data.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Without it the reported disconnects cannot be reproduced or the current connector's adequacy judged.
Retention data is needed to distinguish a connector-retention problem from other causes.

evidenceGaps.gap: Failure location unknown: reports do not identify whether the J12 shell, contacts or harness strain relief released.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: A strain-relief or harness cause might not be fixed by a connector change.

evidenceGaps.gap: No candidate replacement datasheet, pin mapping table or compatibility measurements.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Constraints R1 and R2 cannot be checked for any replacement without them.

evidenceGaps.gap: Exact baseline revision of the controller board not supplied.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Footprint and pinout comparisons require a defined baseline.

evidenceGaps.gap: Independent engineering review has not approved the change.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Release decisions are blocked until independent review and evidence are obtained.

reviewQuestions.question: What vibration profile represents the test track, and can the current J12 disconnect be reproduced under it?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Defined vibration profile and test setup (G1)

reviewQuestions.question: Did the J12 shell, contacts or harness strain relief release during the reported events?
What is the exact baseline revision of the drive controller board and its J12 pin mapping?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Board revision records and pin mapping table (G5)

reviewQuestions.question: Does any candidate replacement connector preserve the pinout and fit the existing footprint?
Who is the independent engineering reviewer, and what evidence do they require before a release decision?

nextAction.action: Define a test-track vibration profile and run a recorded vibration test with retention-force measurement on the current J12 connector to reproduce and localize the disconnect before any connector change is considered.
nextAction.requiredInput: Vibration profile, Rover Alpha unit at known board baseline revision, instrumentation for link monitoring and retention force

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
All sources are labeled synthetic fixtures invented for demonstration; statements are recorded with kind "synthetic fixture" and are not real field reports, requirements or test data.
No measurements, part numbers, ratings or test results were supplied; none are asserted. The field lead's recommendation to investigate a connector change is recorded as content, not as a decision.
Baseline is Unknown; no customer candidate connector was named, so no customer-candidate alternative is included.
